<!-- Included by benchmarks.Rmd when benchmark results exist. -->

```{r setup-text, results = "asis"}
cat(sprintf(
  paste(
    "These benchmarks compare ggumap with the other UMAP implementations",
    "available to R users. They were run on %s (%s, %d cores, %s), R %s and %s,",
    "with %d threads for every multi-threaded contender (umap-naive is pure R",
    "and single-threaded) and %d repetitions per measurement.",
    "All contenders use `n_neighbors = 15`, `min_dist = 0.1`, Euclidean",
    "distance and their default number of epochs. See `bench/README.md` in the",
    "source repository for the methodology.\n\n"
  ),
  machine$date, machine$cpu, machine$cores, machine$os, machine$r, machine$rustc,
  max(res$threads[res$experiment == "datasets"]), max(res$rep)
))
pipelines <- c(
  `ggumap-0.5` = "classic: spectral initialisation, SGD",
  `ggumap-0.6` = "modern: recursive initialisation, Adam",
  uwot = "classic (uwot's implementation, Annoy nearest neighbours)",
  `umap-naive` = "classic (pure R, exact nearest neighbours)",
  `umap-learn-0.5` = "classic: spectral initialisation, SGD",
  `umap-learn-0.6` = "modern: recursive initialisation, Adam (`compatibility_layout = False`)"
)
versions$pipeline <- pipelines[as.character(versions$contender)]
knitr::kable(versions, row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("Contender", "Version", "Pipeline"))
cat(
  "\numap-learn 0.6 still runs the classic pipeline by default; it is benchmarked",
  "here with its modern pipeline, which ggumap's `flavour = \"0.6\"` ports, so",
  "that each ggumap flavour is compared with its counterpart.\n"
)
```

```{r label-helpers}
# Spread end-of-line labels vertically so that they do not overlap: `y` is in
# the units of the (possibly log-transformed) axis, `gap` the minimum distance.
spread_labels <- function(y, gap) {
  o <- order(y)
  z <- y[o]
  for (i in seq_along(z)[-1]) z[i] <- max(z[i], z[i - 1] + gap)
  z <- z - (mean(z) - mean(y[o]))
  out <- numeric(length(y))
  out[o] <- z
  out
}
```

## Speed

```{r speed}
blobs <- summarise(subset(res, experiment == "datasets" & dataset == "blobs"), c("contender", "n"))
ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(blobs, blobs$contender, drop = TRUE), function(d) d[which.max(d$n), ]))
ends$label_y <- 10^spread_labels(log10(ends$seconds), gap = 0.14)

ggplot(blobs, aes(n, seconds, colour = contender)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_text(
    data = ends, aes(y = label_y, label = contender), colour = "grey20",
    hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.06, size = 3.2
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(
    labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.3))
  ) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(suffix = " s")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = palette) +
  labs(
    title = "Time to embed Gaussian blobs (50 dimensions)",
    subtitle = "Median wall time per run, log scales. Lower is better.",
    x = "Number of observations", y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bench
```

```{r speed-table}
tab <- summarise(subset(res, experiment == "datasets"), c("dataset", "n", "contender"))
tab <- tab[order(tab$dataset, tab$n, tab$contender), ]
wide <- stats::reshape(
  tab[c("dataset", "n", "contender", "seconds")],
  idvar = c("dataset", "n"), timevar = "contender", direction = "wide"
)
names(wide) <- sub("^seconds\\.", "", names(wide))
knitr::kable(
  wide, row.names = FALSE, digits = 2,
  caption = "Median seconds per run, all datasets. Missing values: not run (umap-naive is limited to 20,000 rows)."
)
```

## Thread scaling

```{r scaling, eval = any(res$experiment == "scaling")}
sc <- summarise(subset(res, experiment == "scaling"), c("contender", "threads"))
base <- sc[sc$threads == 1, c("contender", "seconds")]
names(base)[2] <- "base"
sc <- merge(sc, base)
sc$speedup <- sc$base / sc$seconds
ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(sc, sc$contender, drop = TRUE), function(d) d[which.max(d$threads), ]))
ends$label_y <- spread_labels(ends$speedup, gap = 0.3)
n_scaling <- unique(res$n[res$experiment == "scaling"])

ggplot(sc, aes(threads, speedup, colour = contender)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_text(data = ends, aes(y = label_y, label = contender), colour = "grey20", hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.2, size = 3.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(sc$threads), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.3))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = palette) +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Speed-up over one thread (blobs, %s observations)", format(n_scaling, big.mark = ",")),
    subtitle = "Dashed line: perfect scaling.",
    x = "Threads", y = "Speed-up"
  ) +
  theme_bench
```

## Memory

```{r memory, fig.height = 3.5}
big <- subset(res, experiment == "datasets")
big <- big[big$n == max(big$n[big$dataset == "mnist"]) & big$dataset == "mnist", ]
if (nrow(big) == 0) {
  big <- subset(res, experiment == "datasets" & dataset == "blobs" & n == max(n))
}
mem <- summarise(big, c("contender"))
mem$contender <- stats::reorder(mem$contender, mem$peak_mb)

ggplot(mem, aes(peak_mb, contender, fill = contender)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste(round(peak_mb), "MB")), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Peak memory of the R process (%s, %s observations)", toupper(big$dataset[1]), format(big$n[1], big.mark = ",")),
    subtitle = "Resident set size, including R, the data and (for umap-learn) Python.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bench +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## Quality

Quality is measured on a random subsample of at most 5,000 points.
*Trustworthiness* measures whether neighbours in the embedding are also
neighbours in the input space; *kNN accuracy* is the accuracy of a 5-nearest
neighbour vote on the known labels in the embedding. Equal values mean the
implementations find embeddings of equal quality, as expected from faithful
ports of the same algorithm.

```{r quality, fig.height = 5}
q <- summarise(subset(res, experiment == "datasets"), c("dataset", "n", "contender"))
q$data <- ifelse(q$dataset == "penguins", q$dataset, paste0(q$dataset, " (", format(q$n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), ")"))
q$data <- factor(q$data, levels = unique(q$data[order(q$dataset, q$n)]))

spread_q <- max(tapply(q$trustworthiness, q$data, function(t) diff(range(t))))

ggplot(q, aes(trustworthiness, contender, colour = contender)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = trustworthiness - trust_sd, xmax = trustworthiness + trust_sd), height = 0, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  # One shared x axis: the differences between contenders are tiny, and
  # per-panel axes would make them look large. Contenders that were not run
  # on a dataset are left out of its panel.
  facet_wrap(vars(data), scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(0.01)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = palette, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Trustworthiness (k = 15)",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Mean over repetitions, with one standard deviation. Higher is better.\nOn every dataset, all contenders lie within %.3f of each other.",
      spread_q
    ),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bench
```

```{r quality-table}
qt <- q[order(q$data, q$contender), c("data", "contender", "trustworthiness", "knn_recall", "knn_accuracy")]
knitr::kable(qt, row.names = FALSE, digits = 3, col.names = c("Data", "Contender", "Trustworthiness", "kNN recall", "kNN accuracy"))
```

## MNIST embeddings

A UMAP layout is only defined up to rotation and reflection, so different
implementations, and even different runs of one implementation, put the same
clusters in different places. Spectral initialisation, for example, can
return each eigenvector with either sign. To compare the layouts below, each
panel is rotated, and mirrored where needed, so that its digit centres match
those of its counterpart as closely as possible: umap-learn 0.5 for the
classic pipeline, umap-learn 0.6 for ggumap's modern one. The table gives the
similarity to that counterpart: 1 means the same arrangement of digit centres
after rotation, reflection and scaling. The classic pipeline's spectral
initialisation fixes the global arrangement, so its layouts agree closely;
the modern pipeline's layouts vary more from run to run, also within one
implementation, so values well below 1 are expected there.

```{r mnist-align, eval = file.exists("benchmark-mnist-embeddings.csv")}
emb <- read.csv("benchmark-mnist-embeddings.csv")
emb$contender <- factor(emb$contender, levels = contenders)
emb <- emb[!is.na(emb$contender), ]
# Each contender is compared with its counterpart (same pipeline).
counterpart <- c(
  `ggumap-0.5` = "umap-learn-0.5",
  `ggumap-0.6` = "umap-learn-0.6",
  uwot = "umap-learn-0.5",
  `umap-naive` = "umap-learn-0.5",
  `umap-learn-0.5` = "umap-learn-0.5",
  `umap-learn-0.6` = "umap-learn-0.6"
)
digit_centres <- function(d) {
  m <- as.matrix(stats::aggregate(cbind(x, y) ~ label, data = d, FUN = mean)[, -1])
  m <- sweep(m, 2, colMeans(m))
  m / sqrt(sum(m^2))
}
centres_by <- lapply(split(emb, emb$contender, drop = TRUE), digit_centres)
# Orthogonal Procrustes: the rotation (or reflection) that best maps a
# layout's digit centres onto its counterpart's; similarity is the squared sum
# of the singular values (1 = identical arrangement).
aligned <- lapply(split(emb, emb$contender, drop = TRUE), function(d) {
  k <- as.character(d$contender[1])
  s <- svd(crossprod(centres_by[[k]], centres_by[[counterpart[[k]]]]))
  rot <- s$u %*% t(s$v)
  xy <- sweep(as.matrix(d[c("x", "y")]), 2, colMeans(as.matrix(d[c("x", "y")]))) %*% rot
  d$x <- xy[, 1]
  d$y <- xy[, 2]
  attr(d, "similarity") <- sum(s$d)^2
  attr(d, "mirrored") <- det(rot) < 0
  d
})
similarity <- data.frame(
  contender = names(aligned),
  counterpart = counterpart[names(aligned)],
  similarity = vapply(aligned, attr, numeric(1), "similarity"),
  mirrored = ifelse(vapply(aligned, attr, logical(1), "mirrored"), "yes", "no")
)
similarity <- similarity[similarity$contender != similarity$counterpart, ]
emb <- do.call(rbind, aligned)
knitr::kable(
  similarity, row.names = FALSE, digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Contender", "Compared with", "Layout similarity", "Mirrored")
)
```

```{r mnist, eval = file.exists("benchmark-mnist-embeddings.csv"), fig.height = 6}
# Digits are labelled directly at their median position (10 classes exceed
# the 8 categorical colours, so colour would not identify them reliably).
centres <- stats::aggregate(cbind(x, y) ~ contender + label, data = emb, FUN = stats::median)

ggplot(emb, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.05, alpha = 0.25, colour = "grey35") +
  geom_label(data = centres, aes(label = label), size = 3, label.size = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(vars(contender), scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "MNIST (70,000 digits), 10,000 points shown",
    subtitle = "Each layout rotated (and mirrored where needed) to best match its counterpart (see the table).",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bench +
  ggumap::theme_umap()
```
